newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - December 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - December 30.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Foreign Ministry denies press reports of meeting between President Chandrika Kumaratunga, who is on a private visit to India, and former Eelam People's Revolutionary Liberation Front (EPRLF) leader Varatharaja Perumal, who now lives in Rajasthan. Perumal, who was chief minister of north-east province, was ousted by rival Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels.

Indian Prime Minister Deve Dowda assures Kumaratunga of New Delhi's support for her policies on Sri Lanka's ethnic crisis. Kumaratunga has proposed a peace plan devolving substantial autonomy to the regions, aimed at ending the island's 13-year war with separatist Tamil guerrillas.

Police sieze another 357 kilograms of hashish from a village along the northwestern sea coast. Police last week siezed over 10,000 kg of the contraband from the same area, leading to speculation that international drug runners may be using Sri Lanka as a transit point for hashish.
Work at the Colombo port returns to normal after a strike by workers opposing government plans to lease part of the port to a foreign consortium.
Concrete slab at mosque collapses, killing six children who had come there for Sunday school, in the northwestern province.
